items.title: Albert Jiles Interview, 1961-02-24
items.q: we was playing together, Albert Boybank and Talbidge, Lester Lewis, from Messmer back Higgins Avenue at that time.

ctx.x: Yeah. What were you playing in, Moran and Burbank and who else?

We played, no, yeah we recorded the record at that time in Moran, but we was, Talbidge, we was playing together, Albert Boybank and Talbidge, Lester Lewis, from Messmer back Higgins Avenue at that time. We was playing there three nights a week. What was the name of the place, Messmer's? Yeah. Is that near the Dandy Inn?
Well that was the Dandy Inn. That was the Dandy Inn.

items.title: Albert Jiles Interview, 1960-06-15
items.q: finally, I meets up with Albert Boybanks, who I played with often and on. But Albert Boybanks made up a band and we begin to get together and play.

ctx.x: Yeah, we're having trouble with this recorder now, but we'll try to finish up quickly so we'll get the rest of your life in here within five minutes if we can.

And I decided that I would make up a band of my own and I would be the manager of the band. So, I made up a band with Albert Walters, Frank Crump, Elwood Theodore. And we went along playing and doing nicely. And we must have stood together about three years. And finally, I meets up with Albert Boybanks, who I played with often and on. But Albert Boybanks made up a band and we begin to get together and play. And then out of Blue Sky one day, I meets a man they call Mr. Russell. And we're about that time that I…
Yeah, I guess the first date that you made was there over at Albert Burbank. Also some with Wooden Joe that year, 1945.
